1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser

  close                       close the browser

  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element

  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab

Storage:

  cookie-clear                clear all cookies

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game inspired by “Clash royle” (assumed to mean Clash Royale).

## Requirements
- Build it now without clarification; note assumptions briefly on completion.
- Make the game playable and responsive, including touch controls.
- User requested screenshots for checks as small JPEGs, viewport no wider than 1280px, and to read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created an original, single-player “Crown Clash” arena battle rather than copying Clash Royale assets.
- Built as a standalone HTML canvas game with card deployment, energy, towers, AI opponent, timer, and victory/defeat states.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable interface and game implementation in `index.html` and `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser smoke test confirmed title, canvas, start overlay, playable hand, timer, and energy update.
- Captured and inspected the latest screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/crown.jpg`.
- Fixed tower scoring so side towers award crowns and the king tower determines victory.

### Active
- Review final changes and optionally rerun syntax/browser checks after the latest tower-scoring change.

### Blocked
- Playwright CLI could not start because its configured Chromium executable was missing; direct headless `/usr/bin/chromium` was used instead.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` after the latest edit.
2. If time permits, rerun browser smoke test and refresh `/tmp/opencode/crown.jpg`.
3. Finish with a brief summary and note the assumption that “Clash royle” meant a Clash Royale-style game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game layout, styling, overlays, cards, and HUD.
- `game.js`: canvas arena, gameplay state, AI, combat, towers, and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/crown.jpg`: latest screenshot inspected during smoke testing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The smoke test started a match and deployed a card; it reported `{"title":"Crown Clash — Arena Duel","started":true,"energy":"2.1/10","timer":"1:59","cards":4,"errors":1}` where `errors` was only the count of body elements, not a browser error report.

Choose a card, then tap or click your side of the arena to deploy troops. Manage energy, defend your towers, and topple the rival’s towers to win. The game includes a computer opponent, touch controls, a two-minute timer, and victory/defeat screens.

Verified JavaScript syntax and completed a browser smoke test; the latest screenshot is `/tmp/opencode/crown.jpg`. **Assumption:** “Clash royle” meant a Clash Royale-style game, so I made an original game rather than copying its assets.
